I'll verify the brief against the actual files before attacking — an adversarial pass that trusts the packet's inline copy is already compromised.The packet's inline engine matches the live `SPINE.md`. Now checking the seams the brief dares me to check — the launcher legend, the dangling pointers, and whether the wiring file actually contains what the trunk says it contains.One more sweep — checking for any "Appendix" remnant that a line-broken or hyphenated search would hide, and whether the wiring docs the launcher names actually exist.VERDICT (3 sentences)

The split is directionally right and the notation carve-back was correct law, but the repoint was verified with a search too shallow for its own repo: two references to the deleted appendix survive inside the trunk itself — one line-wrapped in Doctrine 6, one hyphenated in the Transport Law — four more stand unrepointed in the Deck launcher, and the launcher's legend still renders v4.0 against the trunk's v4.2. The three triggers cover dispatch and nothing else: the two wiring-dependent sessions the boss invokes by name (the lineage review, a spend audit) fire none of them. The deferred restructure was the correct call for a reason the house did not state — today's diff is the control experiment, and pointer integrity already failed at N=1.

BREAKS IN WHAT WAS APPLIED — ranked, with anchors

**1. Doctrine 6's ledger pointer dangles into a deleted section, and no trigger covers the session that needs it.** SPINE.md:150-151 still reads "this shop's actual location is recorded in Appendix A — wiring, not law" — the line break between "Appendix" and "A" is exactly what hid it from the verifying search. The real location exists only in `SPINE-WIRING.md` (`<your-brain>\_claude-brain\memory\model-lineage-ledger.md`), and there is no project-root ledger or `PLAN-CARD.md` in this repo. An orchestrator running the weekly lineage review follows the pointer, finds no Appendix A, and falls back to the stated project-root default — silently forking the fleet-wide routing memory into a second file. What the orchestrator does differently: writes STANDINGS from, and appends rows to, the wrong ledger, and nothing reports the split.

**2. The three triggers are dispatch-centric; wiring has non-dispatch consumers, and the trigger is not reflexive at the point of action.** The trigger "before a seat preflight or the first dispatch of a session" (SPINE.md:871) never fires on two named, boss-invoked sessions: "run the lineage review" (needs the ledger location — wiring) and "what did we spend?" (Meter Law clause 5 demands a reading; the reading scripts are wiring/`mcp-seats/`). Neither is a preflight, a dispatch, a capability selection, or a failure. Worse, the preflight procedure the first trigger gates (SPINE.md:479-511) never names `SPINE-WIRING.md`, and the Deck's load receipt confirms "SPINE inheritance only" (SKILL.md:28) — the obligation is stated once, ~400 lines from the procedure it governs, in the house that just ruled a per-line grammar cannot be fetched per line. What the orchestrator does differently: skips the load on exactly the sessions where skipping is invisible.

**3. The launcher was never repointed, and its legend contradicts the trunk's notation.** SKILL.md still says the arsenal list and color map live in Appendix A at four sites (lines 40, 75, 160, 184) — including the on-invocation preflight step itself: "the arsenal list lives in Appendix A). **Probe the TRANSPORT first**" (SKILL.md:184). The legend declares itself "THE LEGEND — v4.0" while the trunk's NOTATION is v4.2, states "purple now means nothing here" (SKILL.md:58) against v4.2's 🟣➤ transport and bare-🟣 reserve answer — a mark SKILL.md's own reserve-bench section flies at line 122 — and rules "wrap marks not narrated on this trunk" (SKILL.md:59) against the trunk's "any seat that can bill — reserve or house — narrates one on every line" (SPINE.md:852-853). This is the fork Grok's first pass predicted, unaddressed by the applied change. What the orchestrator does differently: renders repealed marks on every reserve line and follows a dead pointer during invocation step 2.

**4. The allowance-enforcement pointer names a file that does not contain it.** The Council Seat Law says "the allowance file's location and format, and the per-vendor guards" live in `SPINE-WIRING.md` (SPINE.md:788-789). `SPINE-WIRING.md` contains no allowance content — the enforcement that actually exists is code (`mcp-seats/allowance.py`, `dispatch-guard.py`; `wmw_cursor_mcp.py` refuses before spending). "Enforced, not merely written" survives only because of machinery the pointer doesn't name. What the orchestrator does differently: a seat auditing or re-implementing the guard follows the pointer into an empty room and either gives up or re-invents the format.

**5. The change record's "three duplications became pointers" is one-third true.** The stdin instruction genuinely became a pointer (SPINE.md:646). The other two got owner annotations layered on intact restatements: "This clause OWNS the consent gate; everywhere else points here" (SPINE.md:66-67) is false — Doctrine 1 gate 1, Doctrine 5, Part VI's dispatch gate, and THE COUNCIL all still restate the gate in full — and "Part I §1 owns the ship rule" (SPINE.md:122) is immediately followed by the rule restated verbatim. No orchestrator acts differently today; the danger is the next editor trusting "everywhere else points here" and cutting the reflex's redundancy. The banked token saving is also smaller than recorded — the real yield is closer to a thousand tokens than to the ~1,700 I estimated last pass.

**6. The Transport Law's "Appendix-A-class" is a dangling adjective.** "Install commands live with the Deck (`mcp-seats/` — Appendix-A-class detail, not law)" (SPINE.md:796) names a class whose referent was deleted; the hyphenation is what spared it from the repoint search. Trivial to fix, but it is the proof that the verification was `grep "Appendix A"` and nothing deeper — in a house whose first law caps claims at evidence.

THE DEFERRED RESTRUCTURE — correct call, misargued

The stated reason — a prose loader "cannot record which modules were read, and cannot halt when one is absent" — is refuted by the engine's own machinery. The preflight already "populates the cast map only from its result, and prints that status in its receipt" (SPINE.md:505-506); the review manifest echoes content hashes; the Deck already prints a load receipt on activation. Prose can record reads, and absence can be made visible the same way meter marks make a missing 💸 visible: require the receipt to name the modules read, and a receipt missing a module-mark is malformed on its face. So the house overclaimed incapacity. But the conclusion survives on evidence the house didn't cite: the smallest possible module split — one file, three action-triggers — shipped today with six pointer defects already standing (findings 1, 3, 4, 6). A shop that cannot keep one module's seams intact through one edit should not multiply modules by eight; the deferral is ratified by the diff, not by the argument. On the deeper question: conditional law is not unenforceable — it is enforceable exactly when the condition is observable in the same artifact as the obligation (meter marks on spend lines) or machine-checked (the allowance is enforced by `dispatch-guard.py`, not by prose). The 12,400-token proposal has neither property, so it should be rejected as proposed rather than deferred — deferral invites it back unchanged, and the 3,300–12,400 range confesses nobody measured. If it returns amended — every module carrying a mandatory mark in the mission receipt, summon-time needs folded into the load receipt — it deserves a fresh hearing. Not before.

WHAT I GOT WRONG LAST TIME — audit of the first pass

- I offered the loader as a co-equal home for the notation — "into the loader (SKILL.md) or a small trunk section." SKILL.md was already a forked rendering (v4.0 against v4.2) and remains one today, four dangling references intact. I treated a proven-stale file as a safe harbor; the trunk ruling was right and my "or" was wrong.
- I blessed the trigger design — "triggers are actions, not judgment calls" — without enumerating the trigger-free sessions that need wiring. Finding 2's gap was mine to name first.
- I counted the consent gate's five restatements as repetition to cut. The house kept all five and was right to: "never self-authorized" is a reflex, reflexes want redundancy, and the Amendment Law — choose the rule that leaves a trace — should have told me so. Taken literally, my dedup push is what would have made "everywhere else points here" true.
- I priced the split at ~1,700 tokens and never re-derived after the carve-back; the actual yield is roughly a thousand. My number stands in the council record uncorrected.

THE THING NOBODY WILL SAY

The council graded its own homework, and the grade fails the Ladder the change re-asserts. "Four cross-references were repointed" — six existed; two survive in the trunk, four in the launcher. "Three duplications became pointers" — one did. The version line bumped to v2.7 certifies that the diff changed, not that the description of the diff is true, and by Part V the description ranks NOT PROVEN. And the file the rot was moved into carries no version line, no owner heading, and no load receipt — the three defenses the trunk insists on for everything else — so the next stale rendering will grow exactly where nobody is looking. The house built a machine for making vendors prove their claims, then filed its own change-summary on vibes.

CONFIDENCE + what would change my mind

High on findings 1, 3, 4, 6 — I read the files, not the packet. Medium-high on 2: if the lineage review only ever runs mid-mission after dispatches, trigger 1 covers it, but nothing in the text requires that, and the review is boss-called by name. Change my mind with: a load receipt extended to print wiring status before the preflight (making trigger 1 reflexive at summon); the allowance format documented anywhere the pointer could plausibly mean; or a ruling that the launcher is out of scope for "the engine" — which would itself need to explain Principle 9.

🟣🌙 Kimi K3, guest seat — second pass
